title: A pharmacy is a practitioner under the Controlled Substances Act
rule_summary: The term practitioner means a physician, dentist, veterinarian, scientific investigator, pharmacy, hospital, or other person licensed, registered, or otherwise permitted, by the United States or the jurisdiction in which he practices or does research, to distribute, dispense, conduct research with respect to, administer, or use in teaching or chemical analysis, a controlled substance in the course of professional practice or research.
exam_relevance: Tests whether the candidate routes a pharmacy to the practitioner provisions of 21 CFR part 1301 rather than to the paragraphs written for non-practitioners.
common_confusions: Pharmacy and hospital are both named in the definition, so neither is a non-practitioner for the purposes of the security provisions.
verification_notes: Read in the current text of 21 U.S.C. 802(21) on uscode.house.gov on 2026-09-11. Added as a new rule so that no released adjudication is disturbed. A fresh independent audit is still required before any section relying on it is published.
